title: Universal property of the integer monoid algebra
statement: Let $M$ be a commutative monoid written additively and $C$ a commutative ring. Write $\mathbf Z[M]$ for the free $\mathbf Z$-module [def-weil-pbc-free-module] on basis symbols $[m]$, $m\in M$, with bilinear multiplication $[m][n]=[m+n]$ and unit $[0]$, and give $C$ its canonical $\mathbf Z$-algebra structure. For every map $f:M\to C$ satisfying $f(0)=1$ and $f(m+n)=f(m)f(n)$, there is a unique $\mathbf Z$-algebra homomorphism $\widetilde f:\mathbf Z[M]\to C$ satisfying $\widetilde f([m])=f(m)$ for all $m\in M$. For every finitely supported family $(a_m)_{m\in M}$ of integers, $\widetilde f(\sum_m a_m[m])=\sum_m(a_m\cdot1_C)f(m)$. In particular, two $\mathbf Z$-algebra homomorphisms from $\mathbf Z[M]$ to $C$ agreeing on every $[m]$ are equal.
